tutorial.home_clock_body: Tap the clock to choose its look from a gallery of twenty faces, digital and analogue.
tutorial.home_countdown_body: A countdown to the next prayer. Tap it to flip over and see the previous prayer and how long ago it was.
tutorial.home_location_body: The city the prayer times are calculated for, taken from your phone's location.
tutorial.home_slides_body: Today's prayers and their times, with the next prayer highlighted in its colour in the middle.
tutorial.sunan_card_title: Surahs of the day and night
tutorial.sunan_card_body: Surahs with a hadith on the virtue of reading them by day or night, with who narrated it and its grade.
tutorial.quran_layout_body: Switch the text mushaf between three layouts: a full page, a card per verse, or continuous reading. The button names the layout it will switch to.
tutorial.quran_font_body: Make the verses larger or smaller with the two buttons side by side. The size you choose is kept for next time.
tutorial.quran_theme_body: Choose the page colour and the ink colour, including a dark page for reading at night.
tutorial.quran_full_screen_body: Hides the buttons and bars so only the verses remain. A single tap on the page also enters and leaves it.
tutorial.quran_search_body: Search for a word with its derived forms, by part of the word, or exactly as typed — or find the verses about a particular topic.
tutorial.quran_jump_body: Go straight to a surah, a page number or a juz without turning pages.
tutorial.quran_editions_body: Choose between the text mushaf and the scanned printings, including the colour-coded Tajweed mushaf. An edition's pages download when they are needed.
tutorial.qibla_compass_body: Points to the Kaaba from where you are using the phone's sensor, and its mark changes when you face the qibla. It needs location permission.
tutorial.adhan_settings_body: Choose the adhan voice for each prayer, set a reminder before it, and turn on the upcoming-prayer card in the notification shade.
tutorial.prayer_adjustments_body: Shift any time by minutes to match your mosque, and move the Hijri date a day forward or back to match the moon sighting where you live.
tutorial.azkar_category_body: Each card is a section of adhkar, such as morning, evening, sleep and ruqyah. Open it to find every dhikr with its repeat counter and its source.
tutorial.tasbeeh_targets_body: Pick the round's target — 33, 100, 1000 or no limit — then tap the circle to count.
tutorial.tasbeeh_mathur_body: Longer adhkar, each shown on its own card with its own counter, so you read and count in one place.
tutorial.library_tabs_body: Move between books, the hadith collections, the hadith encyclopaedia, Islamic channels and Islamic websites from this bar.
tutorial.more_quran_audio_body: Choose a reciter, download whole surahs in his voice, and listen to them without an internet connection.
tutorial.more_tajweed_body: Graded lessons on the rules of Tajweed, and each rule heard in a verse of the Qur'an in a mujawwad recitation.
tutorial.more_downloads_body: Everything you have downloaded — mushaf pages, recitations, books and translations — with its size on your phone, and the option to delete what you do not need.
tutorial.card_subtitle: A short tour of every screen
tutorial.every_launch_desc: The tour opens by itself every time you start the app
tutorial.welcome_body: A short tour of the app, one screen at a time. You can leave at any moment with Skip at the top, and come back to it whenever you like from the More tab.
tutorial.home_body: A clock whose face you pick from a gallery of twenty, and under it the next prayer with a live countdown — tap it and it turns over to show the previous prayer and how long ago it was. Below that: your city, where you left off reading, your khatma, the sunnah of the surahs, and the saying of the day.
tutorial.quran_body: A complete text mushaf and five scanned printings. One tap on the page goes full screen; a long press on a verse opens its card — tafsir, translation, i‘rab and word meanings. From the toolbar you jump by surah, page or juz, search in three modes, and pick the page’s theme.
tutorial.recite_body: Continuous recitation that highlights the verse and scrolls the page with it, and repeats a verse as many times as you set. You can change the reciter from the verse card or the toolbar, and download whole surahs to listen offline from the recitations player in More.
tutorial.prayer_body: Times computed for your location by twenty calculation methods, with a manual adjustment for any of them, and the Hijri date. Choose the adhan voice per prayer, set a reminder before it, and keep a standing card in the notification shade for the next prayer. There is also a qibla compass driven by the device’s own sensor.
tutorial.azkar_body: Morning, evening, sleep and other adhkar — each one a card with a counter for its repetitions and its takhrij stated. You can set a daily reminder at a time you choose.
tutorial.tasbeeh_body: Count with a tap on the circle, and pick the phrase and the target — 33, 100, 1000 or no limit. The “longer remembrances” card opens the transmitted adhkar, and the one you pick takes the screen as its own card with its own counter.
tutorial.library_body: Text books to download, read and search; the nine hadith collections with their chapters and each hadith’s takhrij; the hadith encyclopaedia in seven languages; and a set of Islamic channels and websites. One search runs across every book you have downloaded at once.
tutorial.more_body: Here are the recitations player for downloading whole surahs, the ruqyah, the new-Muslim guide, and the Downloads page — where you see everything you have downloaded with its size and remove what you no longer need.
tutorial.themes_body: Four app themes, separate themes for the mushaf page, and fonts and sizes you choose. The interface is in seven languages, and the Quran in forty-five translations you download when you need them.
tutorial.offline_body: The Quran, the adhkar and the prayer times work with no connection. Anything you download — mushaf pages, a recitation, a book, a translation — stays on your device, and you can see its size and delete it from the Downloads page.
tutorial.sources_body: Every piece of content in the app has a source, named with a link you can check yourself, and every hadith grading is attributed to a scholar by name. The full list is in More › Sources.
tutorial.prayer_card_body: Today's times for where you are, and the countdown to the next prayer. Tap the countdown to flip it to the previous one.
tutorial.continue_reading_body: Takes you back to the last verse you stopped at. It appears once you have read something.
tutorial.khatma_body: Start a khatma, set your daily portion, and follow your progress day by day.
tutorial.hadith_card_body: One hadith a day with its takhrij and its grading. The arrows move between them and the star saves one.
tutorial.focus_body: The mushaf alone on screen with the rest of the app closed. Leave it with the button or the back gesture.
tutorial.quote_card_body: A quote from the scholars’ own books, with the book and the page. Swipe or use the arrows to move between them, and tap to open it full screen.
tutorial.quick_home_body: Prayer times and the countdown to the next prayer, your reading and khatma, the surah sunnahs, the saying of the day and the hadith of the day with its explanation.
tutorial.quick_quran_body: Tap the page to show this bar: go to a surah or page, topic search, continuous recitation, display and edition. Long-press any ayah for its tafsir, grammar and recitation.
tutorial.quick_prayer_body: The Qibla compass, the adhan settings for each prayer, and adjusting the times and the Hijri date for your country.
tutorial.quick_azkar_body: Morning, evening, sleep, after-prayer, travel adhkar and more, from Imam an-Nawawi's «al-Adhkar» with their sources. Tap to count; swipe to move on.
tutorial.quick_tasbeeh_body: Choose the dhikr and the count: 33, 100, 1000 or a custom number, then tap. The phone vibrates strongly at 33, 66, 99 and every hundred.
tutorial.quick_library_body: Classical books to download and read offline, hadith collections with their gradings, the hadith encyclopaedia, and trusted channels and websites.
tutorial.quick_more_body: Full Qur'an recitations, tajweed lessons, Hajj & Umrah, ruqyah, reminders and settings. You can replay this tour from here at any time.

azkar.title: Adhkar
azkar.tasbeeh_lahawla: لَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللهِ
azkar.tasbeeh_tawhid_full: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَحْدَهُ لَا شَرِيكَ لَهُ، لَهُ الْمُلْكُ وَلَهُ الْحَمْدُ يُحْيِي وَيُمِيتُ وَهُوَ عَلَى كُلِّ شَيْءٍ قَدِيرٌ
azkar.tasbeeh_baqiyat_full: سُبْحَانَ اللهِ وَالْحَمْدُ لِلَّهِ وَلَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا اللهُ وَاللهُ أَكْبَرُ، وَلَا حَوْلَ وَلَا قُوَّةَ إِلَّا بِاللهِ الْعَلِيِّ الْعَظِيمِ
azkar.tasbeeh_yunus: لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا أَنْتَ سُبْحَانَكَ إِنِّي كُنْتُ مِنَ الظَّالِمِينَ
azkar.tasbeeh_subhanallah_wabihamdih: سُبْحَانَ اللهِ وَبِحَمْدِهِ، سُبْحَانَ اللهِ الْعَظِيمِ
azkar.tasbeeh_astaghfirullah_full: أَسْتَغْفِرُ اللهَ الْعَظِيمَ الَّذِي لَا إِلَهَ إِلَّا هُوَ الْحَيُّ الْقَيُّومُ وَأَتُوبُ إِلَيْهِ
azkar.hub_subtitle: From an-Nawawi's al-Adhkar and the books of Sunnah
azkar.auto_advance: Auto-advance when the count is reached

azkar.tasbeeh_tawhid_full_ph: La ilaha illa Allah wahdahu la sharika lah, lahu-l-mulku wa lahu-l-hamdu yuhyi wa yumitu wa huwa 'ala kulli shay'in qadeer

azkar.tasbeeh_yunus_ph: La ilaha illa anta subhanaka inni kuntu mina-dh-dhalimeen
azkar.tasbeeh_subhanallah_wabihamdih_ph: Subhan Allahi wa bihamdih, Subhan Allahi-l-'Adheem
azkar.tasbeeh_astaghfirullah_full_ph: Astaghfirullah al-'Adheem alladhi la ilaha illa huwa-l-Hayyu-l-Qayyum wa atubu ilayh

about.blurb: Rafeeq Al-Darb is a complete Islamic app built on trustworthy sources that are freely available to developers. Every mushaf, every translation and every adhan recording was verified at its source before it was added, and every source is listed for you to check. The figures on this page are counted from the app’s own content as you open it — none of them is typed by hand.
about.f_quran_desc: A complete vector text edition, plus {} scanned printings: {}.
about.f_translations_desc: An established translation per language, all 6,236 verses complete, alongside tafsir, i’rab and word meanings.
about.f_audio_desc: {} reciters with continuous recitation, ayah highlighting and auto-scroll, and {} adhan recordings.
about.f_prayer_desc: Prayer times by {} calculation methods, with manual adjustment, the Hijri date and a qibla compass.
about.f_hadith_desc: {} hadiths with their chapters, {} of them carrying a grading attributed to a named scholar.
about.f_azkar_desc: Morning and evening adhkar as cards, a tasbeeh counter with the transmitted remembrances, khatma tracking and the ruqyah.
about.f_offline_desc: The Qur'an, adhkar, prayer times, the nine hadith books and the hadith, tajweed and Hajj texts work offline, and whatever you download stays on your device.
about.f_quran_desc_loading: A complete text mushaf, plus scanned printings.
about.f_hadith_desc_loading: The full texts with their chapters, each with its takhrij.
about.f_library_desc: Text books to download, read and search, plus {} Islamic channels and a set of websites.
about.f_locales_desc: Arabic, English, French, Spanish, Portuguese, Russian and Urdu.
about.dua: And I ask you too for a prayer: for me, for my father — may God have mercy on him — and for my mother, may God lengthen and keep her life. And the same for you, God willing.
about.sources_intro: Every piece of content in the app comes from the sources below. Tap any one to open its site and check for yourself.
about.sources_hint: Where the app’s content comes from
about.src_qurancom: Quran text, tafsir and word meanings
about.src_svg: Mushaf page images and verse coordinates — CC BY-NC-ND as stated by the quran_android repository. Mirrored on our own server, at their request.
about.src_archive: Scanned mushaf printings and adhan recordings
about.src_asc: Enhanced reader voice: speaker recordings (CC BY 4.0) and pronunciation rules (CC BY-NC 4.0) — Nawar Halabi
about.src_tts_arabic: The enhanced voice's models, trained on that corpus
about.src_aladhan: Calculation-method table — the published angles of each authority; and the sighting-corrected Umm al-Qura calendar (High Judiciary Council) for fasting reminders
about.src_musnad_arnaut: Ed. Shu'ayb al-Arna'ut — the complete Musnad and his rulings on its hadiths
about.src_darimi_asad: Ed. Husayn Salim Asad al-Darani — his rulings on the Sunan's hadiths
about.src_ruqyah: A complete recorded ruqyah, from the Internet Archive
about.src_hadeethenc: Hadeeth Encyclopedia — selected hadiths with takhrij, grading and explanation in seven languages
about.src_commons: Wikimedia Commons — the Islamic-ornament backgrounds, public domain or CC0, each file’s licence and author kept in the app
about.src_youtube: Each channel picture is taken from that channel’s own YouTube page and mirrored on the app’s server so the grid works offline. The channels open in YouTube; no video is re-published.
about.src_unsplash: The card photographs on the Azkar grid and the New Muslim guide — under the Unsplash License, fetched straight from the source to your device.
about.dedication: I dedicate this work to my wife, the companion of my road

ruqyah.title: Ruqyah
ruqyah.intro: Reciting the Qur'an and the narrated supplications, seeking healing. The verses here are read from the app's own mushaf, and the supplications from Imam an-Nawawi's al-Adhkar with his references as given.
ruqyah.group_sunnah_note: What is reported that the Prophet ﷺ recited as ruqyah, or was recited over him: al-Fatiha, Ayat al-Kursi, the closing verses of al-Baqarah, and the three protective surahs.
ruqyah.group_sihr: Verses on the undoing of sorcery
ruqyah.group_sihr_note: Verses in which sorcery is undone, long used in ruqyah by the scholars. No prophetic text singles them out for it.
ruqyah.group_general_note: Ruqyah with any part of the Qur'an is permitted; these are the passages most commonly chosen for it.
ruqyah.group_duas_note: From Imam an-Nawawi's al-Adhkar, each supplication with its reference exactly as the source gives it.

imam_bio.bukhari: Born in Bukhara in 194 AH, died in 256 AH. He travelled in search of hadith to the Hijaz, Syria, Iraq and Egypt, and compiled al-Jami' as-Sahih, for which he required the highest degree of continuity in the chain of transmission.
imam_bio.muslim: Born in Nishapur in 204 AH, died in 261 AH. He studied under al-Bukhari and others, arranged his Sahih by chapter, and gathered all the chains of a single hadith in one place.
imam_bio.abudawud: Born in Sijistan in 202 AH, died in Basra in 275 AH. His Sunan concentrates on the hadiths of legal rulings, and is one of the Six Books.
imam_bio.tirmidhi: Born in Tirmidh in 209 AH, died in 279 AH. His Jami' is distinguished by noting the jurists' differences and their schools after each hadith, and by commenting on its chain.
imam_bio.nasai: Born in Nasa in Khurasan in 215 AH, died in 303 AH. He was known for the precision of his eye for hidden defects in chains and narrators; his Sunan is one of the Six Books.
imam_bio.ibnmajah: Born in Qazwin in 209 AH, died in 273 AH. He arranged his Sunan by chapters of law; it is the sixth of the Six Books.
imam_bio.ahmed: Born in Baghdad in 164 AH, died in 241 AH; the Hanbali school is named after him. He arranged his Musnad by the names of the Companions rather than by chapter.
imam_bio.malik: Born in Madinah in 93 AH and died there in 179 AH; the Maliki school is named after him. Al-Muwatta is among the earliest works compiled, and joins hadith to the practice of the people of Madinah.
imam_bio.darimi: Born in Samarqand in 181 AH, died in 255 AH. He arranged his Sunan by chapters and opened it with an introduction on knowledge, its etiquette, and the merits of the Prophet ﷺ.

guide.pillars_1_b: To bear witness that there is no god but Allah alone, with no partner, and that Muhammad is His servant and messenger. These two testimonies are how a person enters Islam, believed in the heart and spoken with the tongue.
guide.pillars_2_b: Five obligatory prayers each day and night: Fajr, Dhuhr, Asr, Maghrib, and Isha, each at its fixed time. Prayer is a direct connection between the servant and their Lord, and is the pillar of Islam — see "Steps of Prayer" in this guide.
guide.pillars_3_b: Giving a set portion (usually 2.5%) of wealth that has reached a minimum threshold (nisab) and been held for a full year, to specific categories of those in need. It purifies wealth and is only obligatory on those who meet the threshold.
guide.pillars_4_b: Abstaining from food, drink, and other invalidators from dawn until sunset throughout the month of Ramadan each Islamic year. Those genuinely unable (illness, travel) have well-defined concessions in Islamic law.
guide.pillars_5_b: A pilgrimage to the Sacred House in Makkah to perform specific rites, once in a lifetime, for anyone physically and financially able to undertake it — not obligatory on those who cannot.
guide.iman_1_b: Belief in Allah's existence, that He alone is the Lord, Sovereign, and Creator of everything, that He alone deserves worship, and that He is described by attributes of perfection, free of any deficiency.
guide.iman_2_b: Belief that Allah created the angels from light, that they are honored servants who never disobey Him, and that they carry out many tasks by His command.
guide.iman_3_b: Belief that Allah revealed scriptures to His messengers — including the Torah, the Gospel, and the Psalms — with the Quran as the final revelation, superseding what came before it and preserved from alteration.
guide.iman_4_b: Belief that Allah sent messengers to guide humanity, from Adam to Muhammad ﷺ, the seal of the prophets, after whom there is no other prophet.
guide.iman_5_b: Belief in resurrection after death, being held to account for one's deeds, and the recompense that follows: Paradise for those who obeyed Allah, the Fire for those who disbelieved and disobeyed.
guide.iman_6_b: Belief that Allah knew, decreed, willed, and created everything — good and bad — before it happened, while affirming that a person still has real choice, for which they are held accountable.
guide.wudu_1_b: Intend in the heart to purify oneself for prayer (the intention is in the heart, not spoken aloud), and say "Bismillah" (in the name of Allah).
guide.wudu_2_b: Wash both hands three times before dipping them into the water.
guide.wudu_3_b: Rinse the mouth and sniff water into the nose then expel it, three times.
guide.wudu_4_b: Wash the face three times, from the hairline to below the chin, and from ear to ear.
guide.wudu_5_h: 5. Washing the Arms to the Elbows
guide.wudu_5_b: Wash the right arm up to and including the elbow three times, then the left arm the same way.
guide.wudu_6_b: Wipe the whole head once with wet hands, from front to back and back to front, then wipe the ears, inside and outside.
guide.wudu_7_h: 7. Washing the Feet to the Ankles
guide.wudu_7_b: Wash the right foot up to and including the ankles three times, running water between the toes, then the left foot the same way.
guide.wudu_8_b: After finishing, say the two testimonies of faith. Whoever says this has all eight gates of Paradise opened for them, to enter from whichever they wish.
guide.prayer_1_b: Perform wudu, face the Qibla, and intend the specific prayer in the heart (silently, not spoken).
guide.prayer_2_b: Raise the hands and say "Allahu Akbar" to enter the prayer, then place the right hand over the left on the chest.
guide.prayer_3_b: Recite Surah Al-Fatiha, then any portion of the Quran, in the first two rak'ahs.
guide.prayer_4_b: Say the takbeer and bow until the back is level, placing the hands on the knees, saying "Subhana rabbiyal 'adheem" (Glory be to my Lord the Great) three times.
guide.prayer_5_b: Say "Sami' Allahu liman hamidah" (Allah hears whoever praises Him) while rising, then "Rabbana wa lakal hamd" (Our Lord, to You is all praise) once fully upright.
guide.prayer_6_b: Say the takbeer and prostrate on seven points (the forehead with the nose, both palms, both knees, the tips of the toes), saying "Subhana rabbiyal a'la" (Glory be to my Lord the Most High) three times.
guide.prayer_7_b: Rise from prostration and sit calmly, saying "Rabbi ghfir li" (My Lord, forgive me), then prostrate a second time the same way.
guide.prayer_8_b: Stand for the next rak'ah and repeat the same sequence, according to how many rak'ahs that prayer has (2 for Fajr, 4 for Dhuhr/Asr/Isha, 3 for Maghrib).
guide.prayer_9_b: Sit after the second rak'ah (and at the end of the prayer) and recite the Tashahhud, then send blessings upon the Prophet ﷺ.
guide.prayer_10_b: End the prayer by turning the head to say the salam to the right, then to the left.
guide.quran_1_b: The Quran is the literal word of Allah, revealed to the Prophet Muhammad ﷺ through the angel Gabriel, preserved from any alteration, and its recitation is itself an act of worship.
guide.quran_2_b: It is divided into 114 surahs (chapters) — Meccan (revealed before the migration to Medina) or Medinan (after) — and also into 30 equal parts (juz') to make completing it over a month easier.
guide.quran_3_b: Many new Muslims begin by memorizing Surah Al-Fatiha (recited in every unit of prayer) and the short surahs in the Quran's final section (Juz 'Amma), then progress from there. This app's "Quran" tab has the full text, real recitation, and translated meaning to help with that.

book_desc.adab_al_nafs: Al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi's work on disciplining and purifying the soul, treating the kinds of soul named in the Qur'an (the one that incites, the tranquil, the self-reproaching), the state of the heart, certainty, and the striving of the wayfarers.
book_desc.al_adab_al_mufrad: Al-Bukhari's book on character and manners, kindness to parents, keeping family ties and good company. He kept it apart from his Sahih and applied a wider condition to it, so not everything in it reaches the grade of al-Jami' as-Sahih.
book_desc.al_fawaid: One of Ibn al-Qayyim's finest books: scattered benefits, admonitions and wisdoms on creed, conduct and upbringing, arranged not by chapter but by the turns of faith itself.
book_desc.al_samt_wa_adab_al_lisan: Ibn Abi al-Dunya's work on the merit of silence, guarding the tongue and the harms of speech, gathering hadiths and reports on the manners of speech and silence among the early generations.
book_desc.al_shamail_al_muhammadiyyah: Al-Tirmidhi's collection of what is reported about the Prophet ﷺ in form and character: his appearance, dress, food, worship and manners, arranged by chapter.
book_desc.al_targhib_wal_tarhib: Al-Mundhiri's collection of hadiths encouraging obedience and warning against sin, arranged by chapter. Al-Mundhiri himself points to the grade of many of them; it holds authentic, good and weak reports alike.
book_desc.as_seerah_ibn_kathir: The prophetic biography drawn out of al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya, in which Ibn Kathir gathered the reports and discussed their chains.
book_desc.bulugh_al_maram: Ibn Hajar gathered the hadiths of legal rulings the jurists relied on, arranged by chapters of law, naming after each hadith who reported it and its grade. One of the best known and most widely studied primers of legal hadith.
book_desc.mishkat_al_masabih: An expansion and refinement of al-Baghawi's Masabih al-Sunnah: al-Tibrizi arranged it by chapter, added a third section, and attributed every hadith to the one who reported it. One of the most comprehensive ordered books of the Sunnah.
book_desc.mukhtasar_minhaj_al_qasidin: Ibn Qudama al-Maqdisi's abridgement of Ibn al-Jawzi's Minhaj al-Qasidin on spiritual purification, character and detachment; one of the central books of conduct among Ahl al-Sunnah.
book_desc.nawadir_al_usul: One of al-Hakim al-Tirmidhi's best known works, explaining principles drawn from prophetic hadith in a distinctive Sufi, formative style. Stated plainly: the book — like its author's standing among the hadith scholars — holds a number of weak and unestablished hadiths alongside the authentic, and should be read with that in mind.
book_desc.nur_al_yaqin: A short, plainly worded biography written for teaching, which became famous and one of the most widely circulated abridgements.
book_desc.qasr_al_amal: Ibn Abi al-Dunya's work on shortening one's hopes and the blame of long hope and procrastination, gathering hadiths and reports from the early generations on preparing for death and hastening to good deeds.
book_desc.riyad_as_salihin: The best known digest of hadith on character, manners and the softening of hearts, gathered by Imam al-Nawawi from the two Sahihs and other books of the Sunnah.
book_desc.sayd_al_khatir: Ibn al-Jawzi's passing thoughts and reflections on the self, religion and the world; among the most delicate writing on admonition and spiritual formation by the scholars of Ahl al-Sunnah.
book_desc.seerat_ibn_hisham: The earliest biography to reach us complete: Ibn Hisham's refinement of Ibn Ishaq's sira. This electronic copy covers only the first two volumes of the edition named.
book_desc.umdat_al_ahkam: A short primer of the hadiths of legal rulings, in which al-Maqdisi confined himself to what al-Bukhari and Muslim both reported, making it among the most firmly established books of rulings. One of the texts a student begins with.
book_desc.uyun_al_athar: A sira composed on the method of the hadith scholars, covering the expeditions, the Prophet's qualities and his life; one of the standard works of sira among the later scholars.
book_desc.zad_al_maad: The Prophet's ﷺ way in worship, dealings, expeditions and medicine, edited by the two al-Arna'uts. Among the most comprehensive works on prophetic guidance.
book_desc.rawdat_al_uqala: A book of ethics and self-discipline in which Ibn Hibban gathers the sayings of the wise on reason, silence, forbearance and good company.
book_desc.hilyat_al_awliya: A ten-volume encyclopedia of the lives of the ascetics and devout, from the Companions onwards, gathering their accounts and sayings.
book_desc.al_adhkar_nawawi: The classic collection of the remembrances of the day and night and the supplications for every occasion, with their chains and grading.
book_desc.at_tibyan_hamalat_al_quran: The manners of the one who carries the Quran, teaches it and learns it, and the merit and rules of recitation.
book_desc.al_arbaun_an_nawawiyyah: The forty-two hadith al-Nawawi gathered as the pivots of the religion — the most memorised and most commented hadith text there is.
book_desc.bustan_al_arifin: Sittings on detachment, softening the heart and the reports of the knowers, narrated by al-Nawawi with his chains — a small book of great benefit.
book_desc.at_taqrib_wat_taysir: Al-Nawawi’s abridgement in the terminology of hadith, a summary of his own Irshad — a teaching text in the hadith sciences.
book_desc.fadail_al_quran_ibn_kathir: The merit of the Quran, its collection, arrangement, script and its seven readers — the appendix to Ibn Kathir’s tafsir.
book_desc.al_baith_al_hathith: Ibn Kathir’s abridgement of Ibn as-Salah’s introduction to hadith terminology — one of the most studied texts in the field.
book_desc.al_fusul_fi_seerat_ar_rasul: Ibn Kathir’s concise life of the Prophet ﷺ, arranged in chapters.
book_desc.mujizat_an_nabi: The signs of prophethood and the Prophet’s miracles ﷺ, drawn from Al-Bidayah wan-Nihayah.
book_desc.musnad_abi_bakr: What Abu Bakr as-Siddiq (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated, gathered with its chains.
book_desc.tuhfat_at_talib: Ibn Kathir’s takhrij of the hadith cited in Ibn al-Hajib’s epitome of legal theory.
book_desc.tabaqat_ash_shafiiyyin: The biographies of the Shafii scholars, generation by generation, from al-Shafii onward.
book_desc.adab_dukhul_al_hammam: A treatise on the manners and rulings of entering the bathhouse and what is reported about it.
book_desc.juz_bay_ummahat_al_awlad: A juristic monograph on the question of selling umm walad, its disagreement and its evidences.
book_desc.al_bidaya_wan_nihaya: The history of the world from the beginning of creation to the author's own age, then the signs of the Hour and what follows. Fourteen volumes in which Ibn Kathir gives the reports with their chains and appraises them.
book_desc.qisas_al_anbiya_ibn_kathir: The stories of the prophets from Adam to Jesus, peace be upon them, drawn out of al-Bidaya wa al-Nihaya: Ibn Kathir tells them from the Qur'an and the Sunnah and rejects the Israelite lore that crept in.
book_desc.futuh_al_buldan: How the lands entered Islam, region by region, from Arabia to al-Andalus and Sind — among the earliest and soundest records of the conquests.
book_desc.tarikh_al_khulafa_suyuti: Lives of the caliphs from Abu Bakr as-Siddiq to the caliphs of the author's own day, each with his history and the chief events of his reign.
book_desc.ihya_ulum_al_din: The most widely read book on the inner life in Islamic history: forty books that walk the reader from worship to dealings to the vices that destroy and the virtues that save, returning every outward act to what it does to the heart.
book_desc.madarij_al_salikin: Ibn al-Qayyim's journey through the stations of the worshipping heart, one at a time — repentance, patience, hope, love — every one of them traced back to «You alone we worship, and You alone we ask for help».
book_desc.jami_al_ulum_wal_hikam: A commentary on fifty of the Prophet's most comprehensive sayings — the best known and fullest commentary on the Forty of an-Nawawi, building a whole chapter of character and practice out of each hadith.
book_desc.adab_al_dunya_wal_din: The discipline of the mind, the self, company and earning a living, written by a judge who lived among people — the classical book that comes closest to what is now called self-development.
book_desc.al_akhlaq_wal_siyar: Ibn Hazm treating himself before anyone else: short, blunt chapters on envy, conceit, pride and the search for happiness, written the way a physician examines a patient — hence its subtitle, «the curing of souls».
book_desc.jami_bayan_al_ilm: Where the path starts: why knowledge is sought at all, how the early generations sought it, and when learning becomes an argument against the one who has it. Ibn Abd al-Barr's collection is the parent book of the subject.
book_desc.tadhkirat_al_sami_wal_mutakallim: The manners of the teacher, the student, the book and the study circle — read before any text, because it teaches how to sit with a book and how to sit with a teacher.
book_desc.al_waraqat: The smallest and most commonly used primer in legal theory: thirty pages defining ruling, command, prohibition, general and specific — and the base of countless commentaries.
book_desc.al_ajurrumiyyah: The grammar primer every school has begun with for seven centuries: without it an ayah or a hadith is read with an inflection that is not its own.
book_desc.qawaid_al_ahkam: «The whole law is benefit»: the Sultan of the Scholars builds jurisprudence on securing benefit, preventing harm and weighing one against the other — the ground al-Shatibi later built on.
book_desc.muqaddimat_ibn_al_salah: The root of hadith terminology: nearly everything written after it on the categories and terms summarises it, extends it or annotates it. The second step on the path.
book_desc.al_risalah_lil_shafii: The first book ever written on legal theory: al-Shafii setting out how the Book, the Sunnah, consensus and analogy are reasoned from — and thereby the language every later jurist used.
book_desc.al_itqan_fi_ulum_al_quran: An encyclopedia of Quranic sciences in eighty categories — Meccan and Medinan, occasions of revelation, abrogation, the clear and the ambiguous, orthography and readings. What a student reads before opening a tafsir.
book_desc.al_muwafaqat: The book of higher objectives: not only what the ruling is but why it was legislated. al-Shatibi returns the whole of the law to the preservation of religion, life, reason, lineage and property, and makes the lifting of hardship a principle rather than an exception — the clearest thing to read on what moderation actually means.

tajweed.listen_lazim: The longest madd: an obligatory sukun after the madd letter
tajweed.listen_qalqalah: The articulation bounces on the silent qalqalah letter
tajweed.listen_ra_tafkhim: An open ra, so it is pronounced heavy
tajweed.listen_ra_tarqiq: A silent ra after a kasrah, so it is pronounced light

hajj.desc_nusuk: How ihram is entered, and the three forms of the pilgrimage — ifrad, qiran and tamattu' — together with the talbiyah.
hajj.desc_prohibitions: The seven things forbidden in ihram: sewn clothing, scent, oiling the head, cutting hair or nails, contracting a marriage, intimacy, and killing game.
hajj.desc_tawaf: Entering Mecca and its manners, then how the tawaf is performed: touching the Black Stone, baring the right shoulder, the quickened pace, and the two cycles after it.
hajj.desc_sai: The sa'i between as-Safa and al-Marwah, with what is required in it, its conditions, and its recommended practices.
hajj.desc_tarwiyah: The Day of Tarwiyah: setting out for Mina, spending the night there, and what is done in it.
hajj.desc_arafah: Standing at Arafah: its time and its place, joining the noon and afternoon prayers, and supplication until sunset.
hajj.desc_muzdalifah: Departing Arafah for Muzdalifah, spending the night there, and then moving on to Mina.
hajj.desc_nahr: The acts of the Day of Sacrifice at Mina: casting at the Jamrat al-Aqabah, shaving or shortening the hair, and the tawaf of ifadah.
hajj.desc_hady: The sacrificial offering and its rulings, the two stages of release from ihram, and what else is done on the Day of Sacrifice.
hajj.desc_tashreeq: The days of Tashriq at Mina: spending the nights there, casting at the three pillars each day, and then the pillars, obligations and recommended acts of the Hajj.
hajj.desc_umrah: The Umrah: where it is entered from, how it is performed, its rulings, and when it counts as the Umrah of Islam.
hajj.desc_farewell: Remaining at Mecca, the merits of the sanctuary and the Kaaba, and the farewell tawaf on leaving.
hajj.desc_visitation: Visiting the Prophet's Mosque, greeting the Prophet ﷺ and his two companions, and the manners of staying in Medina.
hajj.desc_child: The Hajj of a child, of a slave, of a woman and of those in their like case, and the rulings for each.
hajj.desc_counsel: The manners of returning from the pilgrimage, and the counsels the book closes with.
hajj.arabic_only: The chapter's full text is al-Nawawi's own Arabic; it is shown on the Arabic interface.

support.title: Support the app
support.entry_sub: The app is entirely free — this is what it costs
support.headline: Rafeeq Al-Darb is free, with no ads and no tracking.
support.intro_short: This is the only time we will mention it. The app is entirely free and shows not one advert, and you will not be asked again.
support.why:
The ads were refused on purpose: an ad network shows whatever it likes, and an unfitting advert beside an ayah is not something we will accept. Tracking was refused too — nothing is collected about you.

What remains is a real cost: hosting the mushafs, the recitations and the books, and running the sync. Whoever wishes to share in it may; whoever does not has the whole app exactly as it is.
support.free_forever: The mushaf and its translations · prayer times and the adhan · the adhkar · the hadith books · the tajweed lessons · the library. None of it is behind anything, and none of it will be.
support.no_obligation: Nothing in the app changes either way: no feature unlocks, no advert is removed, no reminder comes back.
support.any_amount: You choose the amount, whatever you wish - no minimum and no suggested sum.

hijri_day.hijra: The Prophet ﷺ emigrates from Mecca to Medina — the event the Hijri calendar counts from.
hijri_day.karbala: The battle of Karbala, in which al-Husayn ibn Ali, his household and his companions were killed.
hijri_day.granada: The fall of Granada, the last Muslim stronghold in al-Andalus, after eight centuries.
hijri_day.khaybar: The expedition to Khaybar and the taking of its fortresses, north-east of Medina.
hijri_day.baghdad: Hulagu puts al-Musta'sim, the last Abbasid caliph in Baghdad, to death.
hijri_day.arrival_madinah: The Prophet ﷺ reaches Medina, having emigrated from Mecca.
hijri_day.abu_bakr: Abu Bakr as-Siddiq is given the pledge as caliph, immediately after the Prophet ﷺ died.
hijri_day.hattin: Saladin defeats the Crusaders at Hattin, opening the road to Jerusalem.
hijri_day.constantinople_siege: Sultan Mehmed II lays siege to Constantinople.
hijri_day.mutah: The battle of Mu'tah, between the Muslims and the Byzantines with their Ghassanid allies.
hijri_day.constantinople: Mehmed the Conqueror takes Constantinople, after attempts that began in Mu'awiya's time.
hijri_day.azhar: Work begins on the al-Azhar mosque in Cairo.
hijri_day.jamal: The battle of the Camel, between Ali ibn Abi Talib and those who rose demanding justice for Uthman.
hijri_day.yarmouk: The battle of Yarmouk under Khalid ibn al-Walid, which ended Byzantine rule in Syria.
hijri_day.zallaqa: The battle of Zallaqa in al-Andalus, won by the Muslims.
hijri_day.qadisiyyah: The battle of Qadisiyyah under Sa'd ibn Abi Waqqas, which ended the Sasanian empire.
hijri_day.badr: The great battle of Badr, the first decisive encounter between the Muslims and Quraysh.
hijri_day.amorium: Caliph al-Mu'tasim takes Amorium, after a Muslim woman's call for help.
hijri_day.ain_jalut: The battle of Ain Jalut, the Mongols' first great defeat, at the hands of the Mamluks.
hijri_day.guadalete: The battle of Guadalete under Tariq ibn Ziyad, and the start of the conquest of al-Andalus.
hijri_day.hunayn: The Prophet ﷺ sets out for Hunayn, fifteen days after the conquest of Mecca.
hijri_day.khandaq: The battle of the Trench (al-Ahzab), and the siege of Medina.
hijri_day.hudaybiyyah: The treaty of Hudaybiyyah between the Prophet ﷺ and Quraysh, by which Quraysh recognised the Muslim state.
hijri_day.farewell_hajj: The Prophet ﷺ reaches Mecca for the Farewell Pilgrimage, with thousands of Muslims.

fasting.mon_thu_desc: A reminder on Sunday and Wednesday evenings.
fasting.white_days_desc: A reminder on the evening of the 12th of each Hijri month, for the 13th, 14th and 15th.
fasting.note: No reminder is sent in Ramadan, on the two Eids or on the days of Tashriq, and it follows the Hijri date correction set in the prayer-time settings.
fasting.calendar_note: Days follow the Umm al-Qura calendar as corrected by Saudi Arabia's High Judiciary Council after the announced moon sighting for Muharram, Ramadan, Shawwal and Dhu al-Hijjah, refreshed online each time the app opens. If your country's sighting differs, adjust the Hijri date in the prayer-time settings; the reminders are rescheduled at once.

permissions_intro.title: Permissions the app needs
permissions_intro.subtitle: All optional, each with its reason. You can change them later in Settings.
permissions_intro.location_why: To work out prayer times and the qibla where you are.
permissions_intro.notifications_why: To reach you with the adhan, the adhkar and reminders.
permissions_intro.alarms_why: So the adhan arrives on time, not minutes after it.
permissions_intro.audio_why: To play recitations saved on your device.
permissions_intro.battery_why: So the system does not stop the adhan while the app is closed.
